viral_loop_description: Two weak loops. (1) Share card: 'You're eligible for <exam> — last date <x> — check yours' deep-linking to an eligibility check; rides the existing habit of forwarding notifications into WhatsApp/Telegram groups, but recipients can read the info without installing. (2) Family mode: a parent/sibling is added as a critical-reminder recipient — usually via WhatsApp/SMS (Pro), so it rarely produces an install; it may, however, create a second payer persona (parents) — unvalidated.
k_factor_calculation: Share card: i ~2.0 shares per user lifetime x c ~0.06 = 0.12. Family mode: ~10% of users add a family member x ~0.2 of those install and themselves become aspirant-referrers = ~0.02. k ~0.14 (directional, unvalidated). v1 was 0.12.
paid_feasibility_rationale: India median CPI ~INR 20, EdTech ~INR 68 (Linkrunner 2026 vendor sample, v1 file). Modelled LTV per install ~INR 2-6 (cac.json) -> every paid install is cash burn. ~INR 15K/mo is only a learning budget. Founder budget unknown (no user_profile.md) -> treated as Bootstrap.

platform_advantage.aso_rationale: Unchanged from v1 except review velocity: 'Mark as applied' and 'admit card ready' moments are natural review prompts, but the score stays 2 as moments are spread out. Head terms owned by Testbook/clones; long-tail Hindi/state terms ('<state> police bharti', 'patwari form', 'admit card kab aayega') are winnable. Search intent for 'eligibility check' and 'admit card' is real.
featured_criteria_met: Serves an underrepresented audience (vernacular state aspirants) — 1 of 5

creator_fit_rationale: Audience alignment high (govt-job YouTube is huge), but creators are themselves the alert channel and sell their own batches; the product is invisible on camera; INR 199/yr supports no meaningful affiliate commission (~INR 40-60 per sale at 25-30% would need ~1-3% of viewers to buy). Micro-creators (10-100K) doing 'form kaise bhare' videos are the only plausible fit — pre-submit check content is more demo-able than alerts.
user_distribution_advantage: None identified. No memory/user_profile.md; founder is a solo Android developer with no audience, community presence or vernacular content operation (idea.md).
recommended_first_channel: Telegram/WhatsApp aspirant-group seeding with a free web eligibility checker + share cards, timed to one open state recruitment window; Hindi long-tail ASO in parallel
recommended_first_channel_rationale: Zero-cash, executable by a solo dev in days, and it doubles as the RAT vehicle. Admin-paid posts (INR 500-2,000 per 10-20K-member state channel, from v1 pivot memo) are the scalable variant if WTP is proven.

channels_ranked.channel: SEO long-tail web companion (eligibility pages per notification)

channels_ranked.time_to_first_100_users: days, at INR 20-68+ per install vs INR 2-6 LTV

tier_adjustment_applied: None — user_profile.md missing; tier adjustment skipped and flagged (builder assumed). Raw verdict weak: k 0.14 < 0.2, creator fit low, paid not viable, no founder audience; ASO medium is the only medium dimension. Not paid-only: free organic channels exist but are slow and contested.
distribution_verdict_rationale: v2 does not change who owns the distribution surfaces (SEO, Play head terms, YouTube, Telegram — all incumbents giving the same information away). Precision matching makes the share card slightly more compelling and family mode adds a sliver of k, but the founder still has no audience. Same verdict as v1 (weak), marginally better (k 0.12 -> 0.14).
